doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Radio show on WHN and the move from banjo to guitar
summary: He kept the banjo for a solo radio show on WHN, then in a Bronx theater band bought a resonator guitar and gradually switched, helped by his banjo reading.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well anyway, you pursued the banjo for a while. How did you get into the guitar, and what time was that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Well now the banjo I kept going because I had my own radio show, like I didn’t get paid for it, but it was WHN like in Loew’s State building. I was there for six months all alone, no piano or anything. I just played these solos.

I wish I would have taped some of it you know. Well anyway, from there I got in with some bands, like one was in the Pelham East Theater. I think that’s where, that’s in the Bronx, and that was like they had a girlie show, and we had the violin player was the leader and he played C melody sax. And we had a tenor sax, two tenor saxes, a trumpet player, piano, drums. No bass. And me on banjo. But guitar was coming in. So I got a guitar but I couldn’t hear the guitar. I mean because there was no mic. So I couldn’t hear the guitar, so what I did I went out and I bought I think they call it a dobro. It’s got a metal plate in it. It was a National guitar. Dobro?

Yeah that’s it. But I didn’t know it. I thought it was — but I could hear it a little better because I had this resonator in it I guess you’d call it. So whenever I’d get like a tune that was in C or G, I’d pick the guitar up, and eventually, little by little, the banjo was out and the guitar was in. See I used the banjo because I used to go on in the floor show I’d play “Stars and Stripes Forever” or something like that. But then the banjo went out and I just got to know the guitar. I didn’t take lessons right away on it, but I did have the advantage of reading music from the banjo, so I was trying to find that on the guitar you know, which some of these fellas don’t have.
